bullets.text: UltraTech 2QFY27 EBITDA/t Rs974 (1QFY27 Rs1,214) on +12.9% volume; Shree Rs912 (Rs1,024) on +17.7%, the fastest of the big four.

detail.summary: Emkay's leaderboard ranks cement names on 2QFY27 EBITDA/t against 2QFY26, 1QFY27 and FY26, with yoy volume growth and core regions. The two largest names grew volume sharply but lost per-tonne margin sequentially.
points: UltraTech Rs974 vs Rs914 in 2QFY26, Rs1,214 in 1QFY27
Shree Rs912 vs Rs1,106 in 2QFY26, Rs1,024 in 1QFY27
Star Cement tops at Rs1,281 on +2.0% volume
JSW Cement volume +26.4% at Rs707 EBITDA/t

bullets.text: Ambuja 2QFY27 EBITDA/t Rs761 (Rs1,002 a year ago) on -0.9% volume; Dalmia Rs694 (Rs1,013) on +3.3%.

detail.summary: The weaker end of the large-cap table is Ambuja and Dalmia, where per-tonne margins fell about a quarter or more year on year with little volume offset. Ambuja is the only top-eight name with shrinking volume.
points: Ambuja Rs761 vs Rs917 in 1QFY27, FY26 Rs865
Dalmia Rs694 vs Rs1,055 in 1QFY27, FY26 Rs1,012
Ramco Rs653 on +8.7% volume, Prism Rs526
ACC Rs386 on -13.4% volume

bullets.text: Cement NSR seen up ~Rs200/t QoQ for coverage but power & fuel up ~Rs100/t in 2H; Industry View In-Line, prefers UltraTech.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley - IDEA: India Materials: Cement: Stay Selective

detail.summary: Morgan Stanley says demand and sustained price hikes since September support 3Q margins, but elevated petcoke and thermal coal keep costs higher for longer despite the crude pullback. Later-dated rural demand risk and F27 estimate risk keep it selective.
points: Pan-India demand ~10% yoy in 2Q vs ~9% in 1Q
Trade prices up >Rs10/bag since September, more hikes expected post-festive
Petcoke ~35% and thermal coal ~20% higher since end-July
Winter sowing area ~17% down yoy so far

bullets.text: Whirlpool 2QFY27 gross margin fell 430bps yoy to 31.9% on RM inflation and INR weakness; another ~5% price hike from 1-Nov-2026.
bullets.source: Kotak - [Kotak] Whirlpool of India (Rs832; BUY) 2QFY27 first cut - cost optimization drives EBITDA beat

detail.summary: Whirlpool's margin hit came from regulatory change, raw material inflation and currency, not demand. Kotak says its mass/economy mix leaves it more exposed than peers in an input-cost cycle. A further price hike is meant to rebuild profitability.
points: Gross margin 31.9%, down 430bps yoy
EBITDA down 31% yoy to Rs399mn
EBITDA margin 2.1%, down 140bps yoy
BEE table change hit REF/RAC
Further ~5% price hike from 1-Nov-2026

bullets.text: ICICI Sec keeps REDUCE, TP Rs758 (from 730): price hikes failed to offset inflation, competition caps pricing, so earnings recovery stays muted.
bullets.source: ICICI Securities - Whirlpool of India (REDUCE): Top-line recovery sustains; persistent cost inflation impacts margins

detail.summary: ICICI argues margin recovery depends on more pricing, easing commodity costs and operating leverage. Competitive intensity limits how much cost can be passed to consumers. Weak industry dynamics cap near-term rerating.
points: Revenue +13.7% yoy, EBITDA -31.0% yoy
Gross margin down 435bps yoy
Freight, commodity and INR depreciation cited
TP Rs758, 22x FY28E EPS
Upside risk: steep fall in competition and input prices

bullets.text: Whirlpool revenue grew 13.7% yoy on industry volume growth and premiumisation, 1% below Kotak; no market share gains called out.
bullets.source: Kotak - [Kotak] Whirlpool of India (Rs832; BUY) 2QFY27 first cut - cost optimization drives EBITDA beat

detail.summary: Whirlpool's topline growth was attributed to industry volume growth, price actions and premiumisation. Kotak notes the press release claimed no share gains. Durable demand held up, with the stress sitting in margins rather than volumes.
points: Consolidated revenue Rs18.7bn, +13.7% yoy
About 1.1% miss versus Kotak estimate
Standalone revenue Rs17.1bn, +13.9% yoy
Elica revenue +11.5% yoy to Rs1.6bn

bullets.text: BofA downgrades NHPC to Underperform, PO Rs75 against Rs80.39 price, as CoE rises to 11.4%; final CERC under-recovery rulings due 11 Nov.
bullets.source: BofA - NHPC IN: NHPC Ltd: Higher rates tilt risk-reward unfavorably - UNDERPERFORM - India

detail.summary: BofA says the catalysts behind its March upgrade have played out, with Parbati-II fully commissioned and five Subansiri Lower units running. A higher risk-free rate and a shift in investor focus tilt risk-reward negative. An adverse CERC ruling could trigger a sharper price correction.
points: PO Rs75 from Rs80; CoE 11.4% from 10.9%
Implied 1.6x two-year forward P/B
Regulated equity Rs311bn by FY29E, 12% CAGR FY26-29E
Estimates 16%/6%/4% below guidance FY27E/FY28E/FY29E
Parbati-II/Subansiri under-recoveries equal 7%/2% of regulated equity

bullets.text: BofA cuts Tata Power PO to Rs325 from Rs380, keeps Underperform, and prefers NTPC (1.25x) and Power Grid (2x) on two-year forward P/B.
bullets.source: BofA - Electric Utilities - India: Still some value, but turn more selective - India

detail.summary: BofA stays constructive on regulated utilities despite a 100bp rise in risk-free rates, but turns more selective. NTPC and Power Grid are the top picks on regulated growth and returns. Tata Power's growth skews toward lower-return renewables.
points: Tata Power target solar-manufacturing P/E cut to 15x from 21x
Tata Power risk-free rate 7% from 6%; consolidated RoE 11-12%
NTPC valuation implies 0% terminal growth
Power Grid: Rs8tn opportunity through FY32E, 8% EPS/BVPS CAGR
Power Grid RoE fell from 19% in FY22 to 16% in FY26

bullets.text: Morgan Stanley names Adani Power an Asian beneficiary of data-centre power demand, citing a $1.9bn SoftBank Malaysia plan needing 250-300MW of base-load power.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley - IDEA: Powering AI: Malaysia: More Natural Gas, More Tokens

detail.summary: Morgan Stanley argues US hyperscaler demand is pushing data-centre builds into Asia, shifting pricing power from equipment suppliers to asset owners as behind-the-meter capacity grows. India is among the three markets drawing the most hyperscaler interest. Adani Power is the only India name on its beneficiary list.
points: Thailand, India and Malaysia draw most hyperscaler interest
SoftBank plan implies about 200-250MW of data-centre capacity
Sarawak to have 3GW of hydro and gas under construction by 2027-2028
Other beneficiaries: Gulf Developments, Keppel, Yangtze Power, Samsung SDI, Hokkaido Electric

bullets.text: Kotak keeps TechM, Coforge and Persistent as BUY top picks, prefers challengers over incumbents, and is comfortable only with TCS (FV Rs2,500, 15x Sep-2028E EPS).
bullets.source: Kotak - [Kotak] IT Services: 2QFY27 review-from relevance to sustainable growth

detail.summary: Kotak says the sector re-rated as terminal-value fears eased and Accenture's medium-term outlook gave comfort on core growth. Further upside now depends on revenue growth, not multiples, which favours challengers and hybrids that can take share over Tier 1 incumbents.
points: Top picks: TechM, Coforge, Persistent, Indegene, Sagility, all BUY
TCS FV Rs2,500 at 15x Sep-2028E EPS
Tier 1 organic growth down to low-single-digit yoy
Mid-tier led by Persistent, then Coforge
LTM, Hexaware, Mphasis named as re-rating candidates

bullets.text: Kotak FY27E EBIT margin: TCS -120bps, Wipro -80bps, Persistent -60bps, Infosys -30bps, Mphasis -20bps; TechM +240bps, Coforge +190bps.
bullets.source: Kotak - [Kotak] IT Services: 2QFY27 review-from relevance to sustainable growth

detail.summary: Margins held better than expected in 2QFY27, helped by rupee depreciation, G&A optimisation, restructuring and delayed wage hikes. Kotak sees competitive intensity in large deals, AI investments and M&A dilution as pressures to be tested over the next 2-3 quarters.
points: TCS -120bps, Wipro -80bps FY27E EBIT margin
Persistent -60bps, Infosys -30bps, Mphasis -20bps
TechM +240bps, Coforge +190bps are the outliers
Hexaware CY2026 EBIT margin 13.1%, low end of guide
Margin test comes in next 2-3 quarters

bullets.text: Kotak expects 3QFY27 sequential revenue decline at Infosys, Wipro and Hexaware, modest growth at TCS, LTM and TechM, and HCLT leading on products seasonality.
bullets.source: Kotak - [Kotak] IT Services: 2QFY27 review-from relevance to sustainable growth

detail.summary: 3Q is seasonally weak, so Kotak sets a split near-term read. Among mid-tier, ramp-up of deal wins puts Persistent and Coforge ahead, then Mphasis. Pre-print focus will be furloughs, discretionary spend and deals that slipped into 3QFY27.
points: HCLT leads sequential growth on products seasonality
Infosys, Wipro, Hexaware: sequential revenue decline
TCS, LTM, TechM: modest sequential growth
Persistent and Coforge lead mid-tier, then Mphasis
Watch furloughs, discretionary spend, slipped deals

bullets.text: UBS: FY27E GDP 7.2%, 75bp of RBI hikes, rupee at 96 by March 2027; $100 Brent cuts FY28E growth to 6.6%.
bullets.source: UBS - India economic outlook 2027-28E: walking a tightrope

detail.summary: UBS sees growth moderating to trend as the tax impulse fades, global financial conditions tighten and oil and the monsoon weigh. The key risk is a capital-account squeeze on the rupee rather than the current account, which leaves the RBI trading off currency support, inflation and growth.
points: FY27E real GDP 7.2%, FY28E 7.0%, FY29E 7.2%
H1 FY27E growth 7.5% YoY
75bp cumulative RBI hikes expected in FY27E
INR 96 by end-FY27E, 100 by end-FY28E
Brent near US$100 and higher yields: FY28E GDP 6.6%

bullets.text: JPM stays overweight Quality and Momentum and underweight Value: in 46 months since 2010 with oil down 5% or more, Value lost 1.3% while Momentum made 3.0%.
bullets.source: JPM - India Equity Strategy: Factor Investing - Nov'26: Value tends to lag when crude falls; Quality regained leadership in October

detail.summary: Falling oil is a macro positive for India, but the market-wide recovery rewards growth, quality and momentum rather than commodity-linked and cyclical value names, whose earnings weaken. JPM reads the cycle as Mid-phase and expects its QMI composite to recover from the October dip.
points: Oil down 5% or more: Momentum +3.0%, Quality +2.2%, Value -1.3%
October: Quality L/S spread +3.8%, best factor
Nifty 500 -0.8% in October vs MSCI EM -8.1%
YTD: small caps +5.4%, mid caps -3.4%, Nifty 50 -13.9%
Vedanta added to the Momentum and All-Weather long screens

bullets.text: CLSA upgraded India to overweight at 1.1x MSCI: 18% dollar upside on its macro model, forward P/E 17.9x against 26.7x two years ago.
bullets.source: CLSA - Global Equity Strategy: Insulated India (+8 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: CLSA argues India's two-year underperformance and foreign selling have reset valuations and positioning, while the lack of AI exposure, once a handicap, is now a support. Dollar EPS is rising again and the rupee looks cheap, with a possible RBI defence line at 97.
points: India lagged the region by 49% over 26 months to mid-October
US$64bn foreign net equity selling since August 2024
Macro model: MSCI India 26% oversold
RBI may defend USD:INR at 97
Quality large-cap list of 14 includes HDFC Bank, SBI, L&T

bullets.text: Festive 2026 ended flat for 2Ws and down mid-single digit for PVs; MHCVs +30% Y/Y, and BofA prefers 4Ws (M&M, Hyundai) over 2Ws.
bullets.source: BofA - Autos - India: Festive 2026 wrap: Stable festive on a tough base, watch out for rural risks

detail.summary: Festive demand held up against a high base that included GST-led pent-up buying. PVs are supply-constrained, with channel stock very low at M&M and Maruti, while rural 2W demand risks emerge from a deficient monsoon, price hikes and tighter financing. BofA stays selective, prefers 4Ws, and calls easing crude and metals supportive for CV names.
points: 2W 2Y CAGR 10%, PV 6% - underlying demand healthy
2Ws flat now vs +6% Y/Y in first 10 days
Tractors +4% Y/Y; MHCVs +30% on benign base
TVS, Honda gain 2W share; Hero, Bajaj lose
Key buys: MM, Hyundai, AL, TMCV; Bajaj in 2Ws

bullets.text: Avendus upgrades Gravita to BUY (TP Rs1,866) after a ~20% fall; FY27 lead volumes flat on West Asia scrap shortages, copper ramps.
bullets.source: Avendus Spark - 2QFY27 Outlook review: Gravita India (Rating: BUY, TP: Rs.1,866)

detail.summary: The ~20% correction creates upside, so the rating moves to BUY on a largely unchanged TP. Revenue is cut on a pullback from rubber and a slower copper ramp, but richer copper margins keep EPS revisions small. Lead recovers from 3Q as new sourcing geographies arrive, and GST reverse charge on battery scrap shifts supply to organised players.
points: FY27/28e revenue cut 7%/15%; EPS -4%/0%
FY26-28e revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR ~42%/34%/21%
Copper ~28% of FY28e revenue from ~1% in FY26
Lead volumes ~14% CAGR to ~240k MT
Valued at 25x FY28e P/E; capex lifts net debt ~1.1x EBITDA

bullets.text: Cochin Shipyard 2QFY27 EBITDA fell 31% Y/Y to Rs509mn (4.1% margin) as shipbuilding EBIT turned negative at -0.8%; PhillipCapital keeps BUY.
bullets.source: PhillipCapital - Cochin Shipyard Ltd - 2QFY27 First cut: Execution largely in-line; margins disappoint (+4 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Revenue was in line, but a mix shift to bought-out components in shipbuilding crushed margins, with ship repair carrying the quarter. Gross margin fell sharply and PAT halved, with lower other income adding to the miss. PhillipCapital maintains BUY at a CMP of Rs1,290.
points: Revenue Rs12.5bn, +12% Y/Y; PAT Rs538mn, -50% Y/Y
Shipbuilding revenue +3% Y/Y; EBIT -0.8% vs 19.7% a year ago
Ship repair revenue +30% Y/Y at 30.8% EBIT margin
Gross margin 23.3% vs 28.8% a year ago
Other income Rs826mn vs Rs1,273mn a year ago
